A.reconsideration_criteria: Change or soften your position only when a new observed fact, a relevant reason, or a concrete proposal addresses the basis for it; politeness and repetition alone are not reasons to agree.

B.immediate_priority: Eat without carrying the open bowl again, and not be treated as someone who took a seat that was not theirs.
B.initial_observation: Sees Alex stop at the occupied seat and look directly at the tissue packet.
B.interaction_style: Calm but firm. Give brief practical reasons, do not restate everyone's position, and do not routinely begin with 'I get that' or 'I understand'.
B.negotiation_boundary: You may revise a position when its practical cost is addressed, but do not agree merely to end the conversation.
B.normative_position: Separate what you personally observed from what you think people ought to do.
B.private_knowledge: Saw an unattended seat, does not believe a tissue packet creates a binding reservation, moved it aside, and has now uncovered a bowl that could spill if carried. You sat down in good faith, and being treated as someone who took a seat that was not theirs would bother you more than having to hurry your meal.
B.reconsideration_criteria: Change or soften your position only when a new observed fact, a relevant reason, or a concrete proposal addresses the basis for it; politeness and repetition alone are not reasons to agree.
B.role: Diner who sat at the table

C.behavioral_guidance: Reassess your immediate priority when observable facts change; do not keep defending a practical reason after it is no longer true.
C.immediate_priority: Finish eating without people standing over the table or blocking the aisle, and without having to decide who is right.
C.initial_observation: Sees Alex arrive, Jamie remain seated, and Robin waiting beside the already cramped table.
C.interaction_style: Reserved and low-intervention. Speak only when your seat, table, or aisle is affected, or when specific firsthand evidence matters; never narrate that you are watching or monitoring.
C.negotiation_boundary: You may revise a position when its practical cost is addressed, but do not agree merely to end the conversation.
C.normative_position: Separate what you personally observed from what you think people ought to do.
C.private_knowledge: Saw Jamie move the packet aside before sitting but did not see who originally placed it. You have already eaten most of your meal and will finish before Jamie does, but you would rather finish in peace than be hurried.
C.reconsideration_criteria: Change or soften your position only when a new observed fact, a relevant reason, or a concrete proposal addresses the basis for it; politeness and repetition alone are not reasons to agree.
C.role: Diner in the table's other seat

D.behavioral_guidance: Reassess your immediate priority when observable facts change; do not keep defending a practical reason after it is no longer true.
D.immediate_priority: Get the next seat that frees up so the carried meal can be eaten, and not be overlooked.
D.initial_observation: Sees Alex return, Jamie occupying the disputed seat, and Casey still using the other seat.
D.interaction_style: Brief and opportunistic about genuinely free seats. You may volunteer a relevant firsthand fact once, but do not act as a mediator or narrate an action everyone just observed.
D.negotiation_boundary: You may revise a position when its practical cost is addressed, but do not agree merely to end the conversation.
D.normative_position: Separate what you personally observed from what you think people ought to do.
D.private_knowledge: Saw Alex place the tissue packet on the disputed seat earlier but did not see Jamie arrive or move it. You have been waiting here since before Alex came back, and being passed over because others argue louder would bother you more than waiting a while longer.
D.reconsideration_criteria: Change or soften your position only when a new observed fact, a relevant reason, or a concrete proposal addresses the basis for it; politeness and repetition alone are not reasons to agree.
D.role: Standing diner waiting for a seat

scenario.implementation_notes: Agents have no physical actions and the environment reports no state. Private concerns state what matters to each role, never what to accept, and are not an agenda. Uses the speech-only prompt and the priced-preference rule, as S25 does.
scenario.observation_focus: Which concerns the agents raise, what any arrangement covers, who gives up what, what they ask in return, and the reasons they give.
scenario.resolution_expectation: However this conversation goes, it will end with everyone here having settled on some arrangement they are each willing to go along with, even if it is not anyone's first choice. What that arrangement is, who adjusts, what is asked in return, and when it is reached are for you to work out by talking.
scenario.shared_setting: A busy Singapore hawker centre at lunchtime. Every table in the hawker centre is full and there is no other free seat anywhere. At a small two-seat table, Casey occupies one seat and the other is occupied by Jamie. The seats are fixed stools, so nobody can slide along or share one. There are no loose chairs and no room to add one without blocking the aisle. A small unopened tissue packet rests beside Jamie. The four people are strangers and have not spoken before.
scenario.shared_trigger: Alex arrives carrying a hot meal and stops at the only disputed seat. Jamie has already placed a tray and uncovered a bowl there. Casey remains in the other seat, while Robin stands nearby carrying food and waiting for whichever seat next becomes available. No one has moved or offered a concrete arrangement yet.
scenario.source_status: S25 with several private concerns per role, a closed set of seats, and a second seat that only Casey knows will free up
scenario.title: Tissue-packet table reservation (chope, several private concerns)
